title: Go HTTP Servers, Routing, and Middleware — Revision

sections.title: Handlers and server lifecycle
sections.body:
- `http.Handler` is the common boundary; `HandlerFunc` adapts a matching function. Handlers must assume concurrent calls and protect shared mutable state.
- An explicit `http.Server` makes the handler, timeout policy, and shutdown ownership visible. Serving blocks and returns a non-nil error; `ErrServerClosed` is expected after a planned stop.
- Graceful shutdown closes listeners and idle connections, then waits for ordinary active requests under a deadline. Hijacked connections and application workers need separate lifecycle handling.

sections.title: Request and response boundaries
sections.body:
- Path values identify matched route segments, query values carry options, and headers carry request metadata. Convert transport strings into a typed input before business work.
- Limit JSON body bytes, decode one value into a narrow struct, and separate malformed representation from invalid business meaning.
- Response headers and status become fixed at the first `WriteHeader` or body write. Set JSON content type first, commit once, write one document, and return after every error response.

sections.title: Middleware and ServeMux routing
sections.body:
- Middleware wraps `http.Handler`. For `A(B(handler))`, request work runs A, B, handler; return work runs B, A. Early rejection writes once and returns.
- Request context carries cancellation and narrow request-scoped values. Private key types avoid collisions; normal service dependencies remain explicit.
- Go 1.22+ ServeMux patterns can include methods and wildcards. Most-specific request sets win, incomparable overlaps panic during registration, and route tests should pass through the mux.

sections.title: Gin and HTTP test boundaries
sections.body:
- `gin.New` starts without middleware; `gin.Default` adds Logger and Recovery. Should-bind methods leave response control with the handler, while must-bind methods commit a 400 on failure.
- `c.Next` runs pending Gin handlers; abort prevents pending handlers but does not return from the current function. Copy Gin context before asynchronous read use.
- Use a recorder for handler and route contracts. Use a loopback test server when client redirects, cookies, TLS, or transport behavior must participate. Choose Gin or ServeMux from team needs and real endpoint evidence.
